subject: medicine
intro: Medicine leads to the front line of health care — diagnosing and treating patients, dispensing medicines, counselling families at genetic risk and running the services around them.

roles.title: Family Medicine Physicians
roles.what: Diagnose, treat and provide preventive care to individuals and families across the lifespan, referring patients to specialists when a problem needs further diagnosis or treatment.
roles.where: The course's systems arc — homeostasis, the nervous system, cardiovascular pathophysiology, digestion and metabolism — plus the how-doctors-think lesson is the diagnostic reasoning family physicians use daily.

roles.title: Registered Nurses
roles.what: Assess patients' health problems and needs, develop and carry out nursing care plans, administer care to ill and injured patients and advise them on health maintenance and disease prevention.
roles.where: Fluids and transport (unit 4) — blood, heart, vessels, immune and respiratory systems — and regulation and control (unit 3) supply the physiology behind every nursing assessment and care plan.

roles.title: Pharmacists
roles.what: Dispense drugs prescribed by physicians and other health practitioners, advise patients on using medications safely, and counsel prescribers on selection, dosage, interactions and side effects.
roles.where: The chemical-level chapters (unit 1), the endocrine system (chapter 17) and the pharmacology-basics and infection-and-antibiotics lessons ground the drug-action knowledge pharmacists apply.

roles.title: Genetic Counselors
roles.what: Assess individual and family risk of inherited conditions, explain the genetics and testing options, and advise families so they can make informed decisions and cope with the results.
roles.where: Development and inheritance (unit 28) and the genomic-medicine lesson cover the chromosomal and molecular genetics counselors explain; reproduction (unit 27) adds the clinical context.

roles.title: Epidemiologists
roles.what: Investigate how disease, disability and health outcomes are distributed in populations and what determines them, developing the means of prevention and control.
roles.where: The public-health-and-epidemiology and clinical-trials-and-evidence lessons, with the lymphatic and immune system (chapter 21), are the study-design and immunity basis of outbreak investigation.

roles.title: Medical and Health Services Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate medical and health services in hospitals, clinics, managed-care organisations and public health agencies — managing staff, budgets and the delivery of care.
roles.where: The health-systems-and-policy and epidemiology lessons frame how care is organised and funded, while the systems chapters give the clinical literacy the role's staffing and budget decisions need.
